messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Priyal Kedia

priyal kedia... that's a name that sounds like it belongs on a founder's linkedin or a unicorn cap table

where you working these days?
CureFit

curefit... the fitness unicorn that's trying to make bangalore sweat (literally). found you on linkedin - priyal kedia, growth at cure.fit, ex-headout. 

this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/priyal-kedia-178174328
yesss

growth at curefit, ex-headout... you've been in the customer acquisition game across travel and fitness. that's solid - both industries where you really gotta understand what makes people click "buy now". what made you jump from getting people to book trips to getting them to book workouts?
no, I work on the Cultstore side of things at CureFit

ah cultstore... so you're on the ecommerce side, not the gym bookings. that's the supplement and gear hustle - way different beast than fitness memberships. supplements are impulse buys, gym memberships are commitment anxiety. 

what's keeping you busy on the cultstore side? growth there too or something else?
growth for cross sell - helping cult members become D2C customers via the app

cross-sell growth... that's the sweet spot. you're basically turning sweaty gym people into supplement buyers. classic retention play - much cheaper to sell more to existing customers than find new ones. plus gym members already trust the brand, so the conversion rates probably hit different.

how long you been working total?
2 years at headout, then took a 6 month break and now 6 months at cult

3 years total with a 6 month sabbatical... smart move. headout to curefit is interesting - from travel experiences to fitness lifestyle. both are high-intent purchases but totally different customer psychology.

what kind of role you looking for next?
Business growth only

business growth only... makes sense. you've got the cross-sell expertise and understand both sides - acquisition and retention. that's valuable stuff.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Bangalore but open to remote/hybrid as well
3 years + business growth + bangalore/remote... sound right?

hey priyal - was just thinking about your cross-sell growth work at cultstore. that's a pretty unique niche - converting gym members into ecommerce customers. 

what's the dream setup for your next business growth role?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.

yes
  No dream setup, just more startups - where I can find exponential growth

exponential growth at startups... now we're talking! you want the chaos, the 0-1 building, the metrics that go brrrr. respect.

you're officially in the tal network now legend! 

i'll be sliding roles your way that match your vibe - early stage startups where you can actually move the needle, not just optimize conversion rates by 0.2%. think companies where your growth experiments can literally make or break quarters.

ready to see what the bangalore startup scene has cooking for someone with your cross-sell superpowers? 🔥

hey, capital one is hiring a business manager in bangalore

it's basically growth strategy across product, marketing, and credit risk - analytics heavy like your curefit work

you'd be managing a couple analysts, which could be a stretch but also a solid career step. thoughts?

nice - capital one is a tier 1 move and the analytics focus plays to your strengths

link's live: https://jobs.tal.af/wZmaB

good luck!
But it’s a stretch for me no? I haven’t managed anyone
honestly? yes, it's a stretch. managing people is a whole different game from managing metrics.
but here's the thing - capital one knows they're hiring for potential, not just experience. they'll train you on the management side if they see the right analytical chops and growth mindset.

But it’s a stretch for me no? I haven’t managed anyone
  I’m at an executive role currently

wait you're at an executive level with 3 years? that's impressive - means you're already making strategy calls and leading initiatives.

management of 1-2 analysts is more about mentorship than traditional people management at capital one. they want someone who can guide junior folks on analytics, not be a full-time manager.

but yeah if you're already at exec level, this might feel like a step sideways rather than up.
Don’t match the qualifications or preferred qualifications

you're right - the 5+ years and consulting experience are clear gaps. capital one's "preferred" often means "nice to have" but they're serious about financial services domain knowledge.

your 3 years of pure D2C growth vs their credit risk world... that's a real leap.

honestly? this feels like a "apply if you're feeling bold" situation. the brand is great but the fit isn't perfect.

want me to keep looking for something that matches your executive level better?
Yess, more startups

got it - startups with exponential growth focus. that's your sweet spot.

i'll ping you when my team sends something that fits your executive level at early-stage companies. think series A/B, not corporate innovation labs.

meanwhile, keep crushing it at cultstore - that cross-sell experience is gold for any D2C startup trying to monetize their user base.
Hi
Hey!
hey! what's up?
Not much, you tell me

just reviewing a bunch of startup roles... nothing that screams "priyal" yet but i'm picky about what i slide.

how's the cultstore chaos been lately?
yes please be
always am. i don't waste your time with "maybe" roles.

yes please be
  Bad - I hate it

oh damn. "hate it" is strong.

what's making it so bad? the work itself or the environment?
Both

both... oof. that's when you know it's time.

what's the worst part? like if you had to pick one thing that makes you dread monday mornings?
everything

everything... yeah that's the sign. when every single aspect feels wrong, it's not burnout - it's a mismatch.

you're at an executive level with 3 years, which means you're smart and move fast. curefit's probably too slow/bureaucratic for you now.

what would your dream startup actually look like day to day?
